correctness.rationale: Conditional iid continuous priorities give a shared-binomial representation of the two adjacent ranks. Record-count extension by one index is independent Bernoulli with success 1/(r+1). Exchange-pairing the symmetric tail increment against the binomial monotone likelihood-ratio mass difference proves nonnegative comparisons for all test functions; explicit positive-mass witnesses establish strictness for every threshold 2..n-1 whenever i<n/2. Harmonic means and monotone optimal transport give W1. Symmetry and edge boundaries verified. Independent exact rational Python checks: 6,500 assertions, n<=24 recurrence/tails, n<=12 mixture, all permutations n<=8; no finite test is presented as a proof for all n.

originality.rationale: The new result is a strict, all-ranks/all-threshold conditional stochastic comparison, requiring a nontrivial rearrangement lemma beyond the published exact fixed-key law. Closest full paper, Grübel–Stefanoski (2005), proves the mixture representation and marginal approximations, not an ordering of the distributions for successive key ranks; the known harmonic expected-depth formula does not imply tail ordering. A plausible inaccessible selection-algorithm source creates residual historical uncertainty, but its abstract concerns moments rather than the exact rankwise stochastic comparison.
residual_risks: Older comparative stochastic-order and total-positivity literature may prove a more general rearrangement theorem implying this result without matching its keywords.
Kirschenhofer–Prodinger (1998) complete text could not be inspected; its known variance result does not itself imply strict all-tail ordering.
The closed-form fixed-rank depth distribution is established prior work, and originality pertains only to the new comparative implication.

value.rationale: The natural search-cost question is rank-sensitive. Strict first-order stochastic ordering simultaneously resolves all upper-tail risk comparisons for random BST successful searches and the exact W1 gradient quantifies finite-sample sensitivity; the property is strictly stronger than previously known means or asymptotic Poisson limits and requires a substantive exchange comparison.
